newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey teen sentenced for murder of teacher.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey teen sentenced for murder of teacher.

text.p: A New Jersey teenager was sentenced to life in prison Friday for killing a schoolteacher, whose tape recording of her murder helped convict him.
Kathleen Weinstein could be heard on the tape pleading for her life before she was suffocated by Michael LaSane, who wanted to steal her car. She was murdered on March 14, 1996.
LaSane, 17, of Berkeley Township, N.J., who pleaded guilty, sobbed at his sentencing in Ocean County Superior Court. He said her words would stay with him for the rest of his life.
LaSane must serve 30 years in prison before he is eligible for parole.
Paul Weinstein, the victim's husband, was not moved. He warned the teen he would oppose any effort to win parole.
"My son wants to know why you didn't just take the car and leave her in the woods," Weinstein said. The 7-year-old boy, Daniel, was not in the courtroom.

LaSane was arrested soon after the tape casette was found in the murder victim's coat pocket. She had been carrying the tape recorder to a class at a local school and had turned it on as the teenager attacked her.
On the tape, Weinstein also could be heard trying to reason with him and asking him to consider the consequences of his actions.
LaSane told police he wanted to give himself a birthday present and was looking for a car just like Weinstein's new Toyota Camry.
